items: Interior Attic Inspection: Check rafters and sheathing for water stains, looking for brown or tan discoloration, dark streaks running down wood surfaces, and any wood that feels softer than surrounding areas.
Interior Attic Inspection: Look for daylight visible through roof sheathing from inside the attic, since any gap that allows light to pass through will also allow water infiltration.
Interior Attic Inspection: Examine insulation for dampness or mold growth by identifying matted or discolored insulation and white or gray fuzzy patches indicating mold development.
Interior Attic Inspection: Document all findings with photographs taken from multiple angles, dating each image and comparing against previous inspections to track any changes over time.
Exterior Ladder Inspection: Inspect pipe boots from the ladder at gutter level, checking for cracks, gaps, missing sealant, or rubber collar deterioration that commonly causes leaks.
Exterior Ladder Inspection: Examine shingles while on the ladder for curling, cracking, missing pieces, or granule loss in gutters indicating aging and UV damage.
Exterior Ladder Inspection: Inspect flashing at roof intersections with walls, chimneys, and skylights for rust, gaps, lifting edges, or missing sealant that could allow water intrusion.
Exterior Ladder Inspection: Check gutters and valleys for debris accumulation and verify valleys show visible underlayment or metal flashing rather than direct shingle overlap.

Act on Findings Promptly: Replace pipe boots if your roof is over 10 years old and you've never done so, using Permaboot as a lead-free silicone option that installs without removing shingles for $25-$40.
Act on Findings Promptly: Install Permaboot within 20 minutes from a ladder as a DIY project when you identify cracked or deteriorating pipe boots on your exterior inspection.
Act on Findings Promptly: Schedule professional roof repair immediately upon discovering daylight through sheathing, soft rafters, or extensive mold growth in the attic that exceeds simple patching.
Act on Findings Promptly: Conduct inspections twice yearly in early spring and early fall to catch problems before they escalate into $10,000+ structural damage scenarios.
